name: Saugeen Maitland Hall (Residence)
summary: A T-shaped residence of three slab wings with vertical strips of small windows, pairing two 37–38 m eastern arms with a 32 m perpendicular arm over a communal podium of brick infill framed by deep concrete portals.

evidence.note: Deep concrete portals frame blank brick panels on the podium. Two sunlit brick samples #cdaa86 and #cbab85, concrete sample #b1aa98. Narrow punched openings above.
Daylit close view of the broad concrete head over the recessed podium panels.
Low service wing and a much taller gridded residence behind it.
Flat-ended tall wings and a common core with wider strips of glazing.
Glazing and railings at the podium return.
Three residential arms meet at the central strip of wider windows.
T-shaped upper structure with one slab crossing the podium and two slightly staggered arms running along the eastern edge.
P50 20.17 m, P90 38.29 m, maximum 42.8 m above inventory ground. Cross-wing plateau 31–32 m, north and south plateaux 38–39 m and 37 m, central plant to 42.8 m. Large western roof is near 7 m.

North and south podium edges have six individually capped frames, west edge nine. The cross slab has stepped end corners. The south tower end has a central rectangular extension, with a smaller projection at the east return.

parts.name: Glazed access below the recessed lounges
Lift plant over the tower intersection
Concrete curb under north-west corner bay

notes: The three wings have small differences in floor level. The bedroom windows sit in narrow vertical reveals, with spandrel panels below some openings. Bike shelters are separate footprints c2441 and c2465. The south tower has a square end above the lower outline. Glazing and balcony depth in the sheltered junction are approximate.
